messages:
jamal: quick question — our replay harness numbers are showing a weird 95th tail (~450-700ms) that doesn't appear in the synthetic sawtooth tests. anyone seen similar?
anya: yes, saw that yesterday. replay uses pooled TLS connections but the harness spawns many short lived goroutines. might be connection churn.
sasha: can you paste the harness command + client config?
jamal: running: `./replay-harness --trace replay.json --concurrency 200 --rate 1000`
jamal: client is Go net/http default transport with maxIdleConnsPerHost=100, IdleConnTimeout=90s, no explicit TCP_NODELAY set.
anya: that explains some. default uses Nagle on by TCP. with many small requests, Nagle + delayed ACKs add ~100ms bursts on tails. try setting `Transport.TLSHandshakeTimeout` and `DialContext` options + `TCP_NODELAY` via control socket.
sasha: also check gRPC vs REST path: gRPC keeps multiplexed streams on one connection, so it has less per-request handshake overhead. our synthetic test used a single long-lived gRPC channel, replay replays the exact client behavior including new connections for some users. mismatch there.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: kernel-selection change rolled 2026-01-12 increased p95 by 8% for token length distribution skewed to 512. See /perf/rollouts/2026-01-12.json
mike: kernel selection note — when seq len distribution shifts toward longer tails we fall back to the 'wide-attn' kernel which has higher latency for small batches. The harness inter-arrival jitter was causing many batches to be small so kernel overhead dominated.
jamal: interesting — replay timestamps are real user inter-arrivals, synthetic used fixed inter-arrival. so batching heuristics produce very different effective batch sizes.
anya: action items I think: 1) make replay harness option to collapse inter-arrival jitter (replay-deterministic) 2) unify connection reuse settings between synthetic and replay (same transport settings) 3) add TCP_NODELAY toggle + prewarm TLS sessions 4) instrument KV cache hits in the replay (we saw 15% lower hit rate under replay)
sasha: KV cache comment: hit key depends on normalized prompt + metadata headers. replay harness replays raw logs including some ephemeral header fields (trace-id), so cache keys differ and reduce hit rate. strip ephemeral headers before keying or canonicalize prompts.
mike: profiling: I attached perf traces to the failing run — CPU time is dominated by kernel dispatch + small-batch path, not compute. Call stacks show extra time in `dispatchBatchIfReady()` waiting for timers to fire.
jamal: so the median was fine, tails came from two causes: connection/TCP behavior and batching heuristics interacting with inter-arrival jitter + KV misses.
anya: for client-side pitfall checklist: - ensure keepalive settings identical - match connection pool sizes - choose gRPC vs REST carefully (multiplexing vs per-request overhead) - set TCP_NODELAY for small payloads - reuse TLS sessions or prewarm - same seed / deterministic replay option - canonicalize cache keys
jamal: small snippet for Go transport we used to fix it:
```go
tr := &http.Transport{
  MaxIdleConns:        1000,
  MaxIdleConnsPerHost: 500,
  IdleConnTimeout:     90 * time.Second,
  DialContext:         dialer.DialContext, // with Control to set TCP_NODELAY
  TLSClientConfig:     tlsConfig,
}
client := &http.Client{Transport: tr, Timeout: 30 * time.Second}
```
anya: also for replay harness: add `--canonicalize-headers` and `--collapse-jitter` flags. small change but removes a surprising amount of tail noise.
sasha: one more gotcha — some HTTP clients implicitly enable HTTP/2 when TLS ALPN present. HTTP/2 multiplexing hides latency spikes but also changes how server batches (because request order/affinity changes). our runtime batching logic uses per-connection batching heuristics; switching protocols changed batch locality. watch for that.
jamal: good call. we'll run an apples-to-apples: synthetic (fixed inter-arrival, long-lived connections, deterministic kernel selector seed) vs replay (canonicalized, keepalives tuned, same protocol) and post numbers.
perf-bot: note: create perf ticket PERF-3219 for cross-checking p50/p95 after kernel rollback test.
mike: final tip — always include a tiny warmup with same connection behavior; cold TLS handshakes + kernel caches skew results.
jamal: thanks all — will run modified replay and report back with p50/p95 and KV hit metrics. :thumbsup:
perf-bot: linked run: https://ci.redwood/perf/runs/1766347 (warmup+canonicalized headers)
